oneSecondRead: This square cell is safe buildable ground, shows how neighboring modules connect, and clearly reveals when one local section is damaged.
worldRole: The smallest visible unit of fortress authorship, alignment and future expansion, repeated enough to define the player's home without visual noise.
emotionalIntent: Orderly, dependable and satisfying to assemble; damage should reveal a local maintenance problem rather than make the whole base look dirty.

orientation.front: A shallow structural cell with a clear perimeter, central inset and one restrained orientation cue.
orientation.playerSide: Approved sockets or edge keys show valid construction relationships; no false button-like decoration is allowed.
orientation.threatSide: A damaged state creates one causal displaced inset or broken edge key, never a random crack web.

interactionZones.requiredCue: Large calm central plane. Stable middle value. Color role: primary.

interactionZones.purpose: Show modular snapping and neighbor relationships.
interactionZones.requiredCue: Broad aligned edge keys. Subtle edge contrast. Color role: bareMetal.

interactionZones.purpose: Reveal one local structural failure and its repair target.
interactionZones.requiredCue: One displaced inset corner or broken edge key. Localized warning contrast. Color role: warning.

components.function: Carry the player and every attached fortress system.
Break the top plane into a readable modular cell without becoming decoration.
Explain snapping, adjacency and structural continuity.

states.visualChange: A clean aligned cell whose inset, perimeter and four connection edges form a quiet dependable foundation. All edge keys and inset corners remain aligned. The walkable surface remains calm and uninterrupted.
invariants: Four-by-half-by-four dimensions, bottom-center pivot and collision plane remain fixed.
Edge keys align across every territory and state.
The central inset and perimeter remain the primary top-view identity.
Damage never creates an unfair collision step or changes placement anchors.
Repeated modules reuse identical mesh and material combinations.

states.visualChange: One localized displaced corner or connector exposes a clear repair target while the module remains walkable, placeable and recognizable. One inset corner shifts downward or opens. One connected edge exposes its structural key without creating a random crack web.
invariants: Four-by-half-by-four dimensions, bottom-center pivot and collision plane remain fixed.
Edge keys align across every territory and state.
The central inset and perimeter remain the primary top-view identity.
Damage never creates an unfair collision step or changes placement anchors.
Repeated modules reuse identical mesh and material combinations.

collisionPromise: Keep the bottom_center pivot, footprint and gameplay anchors identical in every generated state.
obligations: Reconstruct every primary and secondary component defined by this canon.
Produce every required state from the same component structure and stable anchors.
Preserve the one-second function, front, interaction, danger and state readings.
Record this canon ID and exact SHA-256 in the compliance envelope.
constraints: Dimensions are 4.0 x 0.5 x 4.0 studs with tolerance 0.005.
Pivot is bottom_center and component anchors remain stable.
One UV set and one material slot maximum per production mesh component.
freedoms: surface_wear: 0 to 5 percent of visible top area. Adds bounded lived-in history without turning the floor into noise.
repair_patch: zero or one approved patch per module. Supports persistent identity while keeping tiling readable.
rotation: multiples of ninety degrees only. Allows layout variation while preserving grid and edge-key compatibility.
prohibitions: unique mesh for every repeated tile
painted arrows, text or false interaction buttons
baked shadows or dirt in the albedo
decorative repair with no causal reason
more than three visible material families
literal construction-toy motifs or pristine molded-plastic identity
